title: U.S. House · Michigan's 1st District
area: Michigan's 1st Congressional District — the Upper Peninsula and the northern Lower Peninsula (Traverse City, Marquette, Sault Ste. Marie).

context.text: Cook Political Report rated Michigan's 1st District R+11 for the 2026 cycle. Donald Trump won the district 59.9%–38.7% in 2024.

Incumbent Jack Bergman defeated Matthew DenOtter and Justin Michal in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote. Callie Barr defeated Kyle Blomquist and Wayne Stiles in the Democratic primary with 56.3% of the vote.

candidates.name: Jack Bergman
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 74.7% of the vote

summary.text: Bergman is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 1st District, first elected in 2016. He retired from the U.S. Marine Corps as a lieutenant general after 40 years of service before entering politics.

background.text: Born in Shakopee, Minnesota, in 1947; earned a bachelor's degree in business from Gustavus Adolphus College (1969) and an MBA from the University of West Florida.
Served in the U.S. Marine Corps from 1969 to 2009, retiring as a lieutenant general; upon election to Congress became the highest-ranking combat veteran ever elected to Congress.
Worked as a commercial pilot and owned a medical technology business before being elected to Congress.

record.text: In the 119th Congress (2025–2026), serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs; Health) and the House Committee on Armed Services, chairing the Readiness Subcommittee, and on the House Committee on the Budget.

candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 56.3% of the vote

summary.text: Barr is an attorney and former high school English teacher from Traverse City running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Jack Bergman.

background.text: Worked as an attorney and as a high school English teacher.
